name: Okeanos Gas Gathering System

values.StartLocation: Na Kika development area, Gulf of Mexico
values.EndLocation: Destin Main Pass 260 platform, Gulf of Mexico

researcher_notes: Not an existing GEM row: no Okeanos entry in the gas snapshot, and Destin (P0175) is a separate downstream line. This is an older, already built line that was never captured, not a new project. An Offshore magazine item from May 17, 2001 says BP (two thirds, operator) and Shell Gas Transmission would build a 100 mile gathering line of at least 1 bcf per day in more than 6,000 ft of water, feeding the Destin Pipeline. The first phase is described as 74 miles of 24 inch pipe for the Na Kika project; the 24 inch figure applies to that phase and the 100 mile total is the planned two-phase length. Enbridge's offshore page (January 2026) lists Okeanos among its natural gas systems, which supports operating status and Enbridge as a current owner; the exact current ownership split was not found. Original BP and Shell owners and a later American Midstream ownership are not confirmed from a loadable page (Hart Energy 403, BusinessWire timeout), so they are left out. Capacity of at least 1 bcf per day is not entered because the sheet has no bcf/d unit; do not convert. Start year and in-service date not sourced. It is gathering, but GEM already tracks offshore gathering lines (Garden Banks, UTOS, HIOS), so it is in scope. Length 100 mi (160 km) exceeds the 25 km rule. Route: no official GIS checked; RouteType unavailable/no route at this stage. Single-origin evidence only for length; medium confidence. Owner name matches existing gazetteer entry Enbridge Inc.
